the EBV immunoevasins v IL-10 and BNFL2a are functionially expressed during the initial phase of infection and that they both contribute to the evasion of immune recognition and elimination of EBV infected B cells.

EBV's immunoevasins v-IL-10 and BNL2a are expressed during the earliest phase following primary infection of B cells, and that both factors contribute significantly to evading EBVspecific immune responses and thus facilitate establishment of a latent infection.
EBV immunoevasins are expressed early in the lytic phase and contribute to the immune evasion of EBV-inflicted primary B cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EBV is able to evade the host's immune response by the expression of the immunoevasins v-IL-10 and TAP-inhibitor BNLF2a.
EBV uses vIL-10 as an immunoevasin to evade immune recognition of newly infected B cells, and BNLF2A to reduce antigen presentation and thereby evade immune elimination.

the two EBV genes BZLF1 and BCRF1, encoding the immediate early transcription factor BZLF1 (EBV-RTA) and the viral immunoevadin BCRF1 (vIL- 10), respectively, are essential for the efficient establishment of a latent infection in vitro.
